newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg, Coke in Nordic deal.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg, Coke in Nordic deal.

text.p: Danish brewery group Carlsberg said on Tuesday it reached agreement with Coca Cola Company on a joint venture project for production and distribution of soft drinks in Denmark and Sweden.
Carlsberg said in a statement that the deal covered Coca Cola and other soft drinks and was a natural extension of already long-existing cooperation in Denmark through Carlsberg-owned A/S Dadeko.

It said that the first stage of the joint venture deal would be to set up a new Coca Cola Nordic Beverages A/S (CCNB) holding company, 51 percent owned by Carlsberg and 49 percent by the Coca Cola Company.

The intention is that CCNB, with headquarters in Copenhagen, will act as holding company for units in the separate countries which are licensed to produce, sell and distribute Coca Cola products including the Coca Cola, Coca Cola Light, Fanta and Sprite soft drink brands, it said.

In Denmark Carlsberg's wholly-owned A/S Dadeko subsidiary, which has hitherto produced and marketed Coca Cola products in the country, will be placed under the new holding company in return for a 51 percent shareholding in CCNB, it said.

In Sweden, the Cola Cola Company will contribute to the new entity with its 100 percent-owned Coca Cola Drycker Sverige AB (CCDS) along with an unspecified capital contribution in exchange for a 49 percent shareholding in CCNB, it said.
A separate distribution agreement in Sweden had been signed between CCDS and local Falcon Bryggerier AB in which Carlsberg holds a 50 percent stake, it added.
As regards Norway, Carlsberg said it was still being considered whether Coca Cola Beverages Norway AS would also become part of the new CCNB holding company.
